messages:
alice: Heads up — after last night's RBAC migration some customers report SCIM failures for a subset of users. Getting 422s with "external_id validation failed" and sporadic KMS decrypt errors in the provisioning worker. Anyone seen this pattern before?

bob: ugh. which orgs? any common IdP?

alice: two large enterprise tenants on AAD + one on Okta. error sample from logs: 
```
2026-03-14T03:12:07Z provisioning-worker ERROR user=svc-scim request_id=abc123 extid_blob_decrypt failed: kms.Decrypt: invalid context (SignatureMismatch)
HTTP 422 SCIM /Users - body: {"detail":"external_id validation failed"}
```

charlie: SignatureMismatch from KMS usually means the AAD/Okta extid blob was re-encrypted with a different key or context changed. Did the RBAC migration include any extid hashing or name-format changes?

alice: we did change how we render the SCIM external_id for role-scoped service accounts — switched from `email|uid` to `sha256(email|uid)` to de-duplicate across renames. That change was gated, but maybe a rollout step hit prod early for some orgs.

diane: oh. that will break decryption if we changed the KMS encryption context key used to build the ciphertext. We sign with `extid:v1` in the context. Did the migration bump that to `extid:v2`?

alice: not intentionally. config shows `scim.extid_version` still v1 in the feature flags for the orgs, but the new provisioning lambda (deployed in the same deploy) has default v2 when flag missing. Might be a flag-eval bug.

oncall: rolling up: failures = (a) decrypt errors in KMS; (b) SCIM returning 422 external_id validation; (c) users not being created/updated. Impact: provisioning backlog for 3 customers, manual invites needed.

bob: can we reproduce locally by re-encrypting with v2 context and having the worker try to decrypt with v1? I can script a quick repro.

charlie: also check SAML NameID/NameFormat changes. If extid is derived from the NameID, and IdP started returning `transient` vs `persistent`, extid hash won't match. Did we see any SAML assertion changes in the SSO logs?

alice: good call — SSO logs show Okta tenant sent NameID Format urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent for most users, but ~20% had `emailAddress` in the assertion yesterday. Could be a user directory migration at customer side.

diane: TL;DR we have two orthogonal causes: provider-side NameID format flips and our rollout defaulting extid version to v2 when feature flag absent. Combined they produce un-decryptable extid blobs.

oncall: mitigation plan?

bob: immediate: add a defensive fallback in the provisioning worker — if KMS decrypt returns SignatureMismatch, try alternate contexts (extid:v2 and extid:v1) then attempt a best-effort parse. Also add a metric + alert for decrypt signature mismatch spike.

charlie: agree. add a temporary compatibility mode that accepts both `sha256` and legacy plaintext extid, and avoids rejecting with 422 if we can map to an existing user by other attributes (email, external_username). We'll log high-fidelity audit entries for repro.

alice: I'm going to patch the feature-flag evaluation so default stays v1 unless org explicitly opted in. Rolling that now to staging.

diane: ops checklist: 1) patch worker fallback; 2) rollout flag fix; 3) run a migration job to reconcile v2 blobs (re-encrypt into v1) for affected orgs only after explicit customer approval; 4) notify customers and provide manual invite instructions.

oncall: please also capture an incident timeline and add the affected user list for compliance/audit. This crosses our SCIM SLA.

bob: repro script: 
```
# simulate v2 encryption then attempt v1 decrypt
python tools/kms_repro.py --encrypt-context extid:v2 --decrypt-context extid:v1 --payload "test@example.com|123"
```
Produces `kms.Decrypt: SignatureMismatch` as expected.

charlie: For postmortem we should include: how flag eval defaulted, why deploy contained default change, why our canary didn't catch it (canary uses orgs that had explicit flags set), and add a unit test for fallback contexts.

alice: I've notified the two PMs for the customers and started the rollback of the default in staging. Will push the worker fallback hotfix to prod in the next 30m with an emergency rollback plan.

diane: I'll open a KMS runbook ticket — need to coordinate key policy / re-encrypt permissions if we do a mass reconcile. Also confirm HSM audit entries for these decrypt failures for compliance.

oncall: adding action items to the incident doc: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-0032 (will update).

bob: small follow-up — if IdP switches NameFormat frequently, we should make external_id derivation deterministic using NameID canonicalization rules + fallback to stable claims (like sub or immutable id). Add to backlog: external_id resilience RFC.

alice: agreed. I'll own the RFC. Thanks team — let's keep this thread for updates, and ping me with deploy links. :thumbsup:
